messages:
raj: Heads up — during the eu-west-2 firewall tighten rollout we just flipped, ~28% of new GPU nodes failed onboarding. Keystore decrypts timing out, joins stuck. Anyone oncall?

maria: on it, pinging keystore team. can you paste the node error and the exact acl that changed?

raj: Error excerpt from kubelet logs: 
```
2026-03-21T14:02:01Z keystore: decrypt timeout after 5s: rpc error: code=Unavailable desc = connection closed by peer
node-controller: gpu-node-27 failed to register: keystore decrypt error
```
The ACL change was: deny 0.0.0.0/0 outbound from worker-subnet -> allowed only to keystore privatelink endpoint and cloudwatch. Previously NAT was allowed.

kelly: oof. sounds like nodes were still relying on NAT egress to reach the keystore cluster (we had a fallback path). when you tightened, the fallback path got cut. Can you confirm if the keystore privatelink is in the same AZ?

raj: privatelink exists but is in a subset of subnets (control plane only). Some GPUs try to reach a regional keystore recorder (for KMS unseal) over public IPs. Knee-jerk config change removed that path.

sasha: quick triage idea: temporarily re-open NAT egress for the worker-subnet (restrict to keystore IPs) while we migrate nodes to use privatelink-only DNS. That avoids cross-region routing. But NAT egress has cost implications, especially for 500+ TB egress/month if we hold it.

ops-oncall: If we re-open NAT we'll see immediate onboarding success. I'm +1 for temporary re-open for 30m and then rotate nodes to privatelink. But we should also instrument keystore clients to cache decrypts for longer to reduce KMS QPS.

maria: Also noticed increase in KMS audit log sampling last week — the auditshipper changed sampling from 10% -> 100% in eu-west-2 (was an accidental flag). That pushed keystore proxies harder and increased latency. Combined with the ACL change, nodes hit the decrypt timeout. Rolling back sampling may help.

raj: good catch. @maria, can you reduce sampling and re-validate? If we do both (sampling rollback + NAT for 30m) we should clear the join backlog without larger cost.

maria: reducing audit sampling now. command: `kubectl -n infra set env daemonset/audit-shipper SAMPLE_RATE=0.1`

infra-bot: deploy-bot: audit-shipper: patch applied by maria — rollout in progress (3/3 pods updated).

kelly: i triggered a quick NAT allow rule: `aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-abc123 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --gateway-id nat-xxxxx` (restricted to keystore IP ranges via security group). nodes started registering within 90s.

raj: Confirmed — onboarding success rate back to ~98% in last 5 mins. Remaining failures look like stale instances that never retried.

ops-oncall: plan going forward: 1) keep NAT allow for 30m, 2) migrate node bootstrap to privatelink-only endpoint (DNS + IAM role check), 3) add keystore client local caching (TTL 10m) to reduce KMS QPS, 4) add a canary ACL change runbook and preflight that checks a sample of nodes for egress dependency.

sasha: +1. Also we should consider ephemeral key TTL + batching at the keystore to reduce decrypt frequency. Cost note: temporary NAT allow is ~€0.60/hr for the NAT GW + egress charges depending on volume. If we do this frequently, monthly costs will spike.

maria: I'm going to open a ticket to revert the audit sampling rollout and add a guard so that sampling can't be set to >20% without a runbook.

raj: Thanks. Will monitor onboarding for the next hour and then close the NAT route. If anything else pops up I’ll @ops-oncall.

kelly: Logged the action: `infra-notes: 5167890123 — temporary NAT allow applied -> nodes recovered; audit sampling rolled back; followups: keystore client TTL, privatelink DNS migration, canary ACL preflight`

ops-oncall: adding task to backlog and pinging finance for a quick cost estimate of a 6-hr NAT re-open if we need it.

maria: FYI auditshipper change looks like it was an automated config flip from a test pipeline — tracking owner. will add tighter gating.

raj: resolved for now. thanks all :thumbsup:
